column1: # OWASP ZAP baseline rule configuration (plan task 46, T14).
# Format, tab separated:  <rule id>
# This file is a review record, not a way to quieten the scanner. Every IGNORE below names why the finding is
# a deliberate decision and which test holds that decision in place; anything not listed is reported, and
# scripts/check_zap_report.py fails the build on Medium or higher.
# What the scan actually reports, from the first CI run of this workflow (ZAP 2.17.0, the app in Production):
# nothing at Medium or above, and check_zap_report.py graded the report 3 Low and 8 Informational. One rule is
# suppressed, 10109 below. The other four are left reported rather than suppressed — they are below the gate,
# and a Low that turns into something worse should not already be on an allowlist:
#   10049 Non-Storable Content   — the secret paths send no-store and Pragma: no-cache precisely so a
#                                  plaintext page never reaches a cache. ZAP notes the absence of storability;
#                                  that absence is the mitigation (T9).
#   10094 Base64 Disclosure      — the base64 it finds is the bundle's SRI integrity attribute and the CSP
#                                  script-src hash, both public by construction (T7).
#   90004 Site isolation         — Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy, -Opener-Policy and -Resource-Policy are not
#                                  set. Real, small and outside this task, which adds CI rather than changing
#                                  what the app sends; the response headers live in Security/SecurityHeaders.cs.
#   90005 Sec-Fetch-Dest missing — a property of ZAP's own requests, not of the app's responses.
# An earlier note here recorded "exactly one alert, no Low", from a hand-driven run over 15 listed URLs. The
# baseline action also spiders, so it reaches robots.txt, sitemap.xml and favicon.ico and sees more. The CI
# run is the one that counts.

column3: Modern Web Application: ZAP noting the page is script-driven, which is the design (client-side AES-GCM, T1). Not a finding. The one script it sees is the first-party bundle, pinned by SRI and the CSP script-src hash and checked by BundleIntegrityTests and headers.spec.ts.
